name: The Gilded Lie
summary: Chapter 3 of The Seven Teeth of Vashkul. The trail of plague grain leads to Highcrown's golden salons and the Royal Almoner, Lady Seraphine Vell. The hero must assemble proof against her, beat Vosk the Hollow to the Sky Tooth and the lost lance Dawnbreaker at Old Vaelthorn, survive the Choir's assassins at Dawnspire, and unmask the Cantor at her own midsummer masque, then choose between saving the poisoned Queen and pursuing the Cantor.

chapters.name: The Gilded Lie
chapters.summary: Court intrigue in Aurelmark: the Almoner, the lance, the masque and the poisoned Queen.

scenes.name: An Audience in the Tower Hall
scenes.seed: Highcrown climbs its hill in white tiers, banners of the golden crown on every tower. In the Tower Hall, Queen Isolde Varannis holds audience beneath a ceiling painted with the Dawn Lance's old victories. At her side stands Lady Seraphine Vell, the Royal Almoner, in plain grey, beloved by every beggar in the lower city.

variants.seed: Wanted posters bearing your likeness are pasted beside the Queen's Gate, and a knight of the watch is checking every face in the queue.
You are inside the walls, but you are still a wanted face in Highcrown.
Fen refugees from burned Hollowmere camp below the lower gate, and the Almonry feeds them first.
Criers in the market repeat the news from the fen: Hollowmere was cured, not burned.
A Saltwind Company pennant flies over the harbor-guild hall; the Company has written ahead to praise you.
Courtiers whisper that you sailed with Red Gull pirates. Chamberlain Hale has not stopped watching you.
Broadsheets in the market tell how Governor Pell was exposed in Port Sorrel, and some of them name you.
A dockside rumour says Harrow Vey's grey ship was seen on the river below the city.
You have heard the Choir hymn hummed in the lower city twice today. The Choir is stronger here than anyone admits.
Ser Corwin straightens his dismissed-knight's tabard every time a Dawn Lance banner passes.
Nettle glares at the marble as if it owes the fen money.
Rook is admiring the courtiers' purses with professional interest.
The royal warrant in your belt opens doors all over the city.

onEnter.text: Queen Isolde's summons has brought you to Highcrown, the white capital. The court will receive you in the Tower Hall.

actions.label: Bluff your way past the gate watch

success.text: You are a wool-merchant from Brightwater with a bad cough, and the knight waves you through before you can cough on him.

failure.text: The knight compares your face to the poster, twice. "Seize them."

actions.label: Slip in with a wine cart

success.text: You ride into Highcrown under a tarpaulin and three casks of Brightwater red.

failure.text: A watchman prods the tarpaulin with his halberd and finds you under it.

actions.label: Let Ser Corwin vouch for you

outcome.text: Corwin gives the watch-knight his name and his word. The knight served under him once, and the gate opens.

actions.label: Fight your way through the Queen's Gate

outcome.text: You draw steel in the Queen's Gate. The watch closes in.

actions.label: Bribe a turnkey (150 gp)

outcome.text: One hundred and fifty gold buys a forgotten door and a turnkey with a bad memory.

actions.label: Break out of the Highcrown dungeons

success.text: You work a rusted bar loose and climb out through a drain into the lower city.

failure.text: The bars hold. A guard bangs his keys on them to make sure you know it.

actions.label: Wait for the Queen to hear your case

outcome.text: Three days in a Highcrown cell, and then two guards march you to the Tower Hall to plead your case in chains.

actions.label: Attend the Queen's audience

outcome.text: Queen Isolde hears your tale of the Choir and the Teeth without interrupting once. Lady Seraphine offers "the Almonry's full aid", and asks, very gently, whether you would let the Almonry keep any Teeth "for safekeeping". The Queen's scouts report Choir climbers on the sky-towers of Old Vaelthorn, where the lance Dawnbreaker was lost.

actions.label: Ask the Queen for a royal warrant to investigate

success.text: Isolde signs and seals a royal warrant with her own hand: every door in the kingdom is to open to you, for the length of this inquiry.

failure.text: Chamberlain Hale reminds the Queen that warrants are "not for strangers", and your request goes to a committee.

actions.label: Ask the Queen for a royal warrant despite the pirate rumours

success.text: The Queen studies you a long time, then signs the warrant anyway. "The Red Gulls owe me a fleet. Perhaps you will be the one to collect it."

failure.text: "A friend of pirates asks me for a warrant," Hale says to no one in particular. The Queen declines.

actions.label: Plead with the Queen for a pardon

success.text: Isolde strikes your name from the wanted rolls with one stroke of her pen. "Earn it," she says.

failure.text: The Queen will not pardon you, but she will let you walk out of her hall. Once.

actions.label: Plead with the Queen for a pardon despite the pirate rumours

success.text: Against all the Chamberlain's advice, Isolde strikes your name from the wanted rolls. "Earn it."

failure.text: An outlaw who sails with pirates, asking for mercy? The Queen will let you walk out of her hall. Once.

actions.label: Watch Lady Seraphine closely

success.text: Seraphine's eyes go to your pack every time the Teeth are mentioned, and her kindness never quite reaches them. She is far too interested in the Teeth.

failure.text: You see only a tired, kind woman who has fed half the kingdom.

actions.label: Entrust a Tooth to the Almonry for safekeeping

outcome.text: Seraphine takes the Tooth in both hands as if it were a child, and a clerk carries it away to the Almonry vaults. "It will be quite safe with me," she says.

actions.label: Hear out the young scholar Aurek Vell

success.text: Aurek talks in footnotes about "strange readings" in his aunt's library, and by the end of it he has asked, very politely, to come with you.

failure.text: Aurek loses his nerve halfway through a sentence, apologises, and retreats to the Almonry library. He might be persuaded by something he can study.

actions.label: Hear out the young scholar Aurek Vell

success.text: Aurek has heard you sail with pirates, and has decided that is "rather thrilling". He asks to come with you.

failure.text: Aurek is too nervous of a pirate's friend to say much. He might be persuaded by something he can study.

actions.label: Show Aurek a Tooth

outcome.text: "It's in my aunt's books!" Aurek forgets to be shy entirely. He will not let the Tooth out of his sight now, and he is coming with you.

exits.label: Take the mountain road to Deepanvil Hold
Ride for the Ruins of Old Vaelthorn
Go to the Almoner's midsummer masque

scenes.name: The Counting-Halls of Deepanvil
scenes.seed: Deepanvil Hold rings with hammers and the clack of counting-frames. In the Ironvault's counting-hall, Guildmistress Brunhild Ashgrove keeps the Crown's debts in iron-bound ledgers, and she keeps them closed.

variants.seed: Ashgrove has a list of Red Gull raids on Consortium ore-ships, and your name is written at the bottom of it.
A Saltwind factor is at Ashgrove's elbow, and he greets you as a friend of the Company.
The Guildmistress eyes your royal warrant the way a smith eyes a cracked blade.
The miners toast you in the tavern: the sealed deep mine is open again.
The Almonry's debts lie open on the table, tallied in your hand.

onEnter.text: Ashgrove will talk about the Almonry's borrowing, but she will open the ledgers only if the Crown's overdue debt is settled, or for a favor: "diggers in black" have broken into the sealed deep mine, and the Consortium wants it back.

actions.label: Pay the Consortium 300 gp restitution for the Red Gull raids

outcome.text: Three hundred gold, counted twice. Ashgrove writes "settled" in the margin, and now she will deal with you.

actions.label: Argue that you owe the Consortium nothing

success.text: You point out that the Red Gulls sank Choir ships, not Consortium ones, and prove it. Ashgrove grunts and strikes the line.

failure.text: "Coin first, then talk," says the Guildmistress, and turns back to her ledgers.

actions.label: Present the Saltwind Company's letter of credit

outcome.text: The Company underwrites the Crown's arrears in your name. Ashgrove, who never refuses good paper, unlocks the ledgers.

actions.label: Clear the sealed deep mine for the Consortium

outcome.text: Miners lower you into the sealed deep mine. Things with no eyes are waiting in the dark, and something is eating the rails.

actions.label: Persuade Ashgrove to open the ledgers

success.text: You convince Ashgrove the Almonry's debts are the Consortium's danger too. She opens the ledgers herself.

failure.text: "The Consortium's books are the Consortium's business," says Ashgrove.

actions.label: Open the ledgers by royal warrant

success.text: The Queen's seal opens the ledgers. Ashgrove will not forget that you used it on her.

failure.text: Ashgrove reads the warrant and asks which clause obliges a dwarven guild to anything. You cannot find one.

actions.label: Take the Consortium's reward: a dwarven war hammer

outcome.text: Ashgrove presents a dwarven thrower from the Ironvault armory, runes still warm from the forge.

actions.label: Take the Consortium's reward: adamantine armor

outcome.text: Ashgrove's smiths fit you with adamantine armor, as fine as anything in the Ironvault.

actions.label: Study the Almonry's ledgers

success.text: The ledgers tell it plainly once you see it: the Almonry has borrowed a fortune against the royal seal, and the money runs to Port Sorrel grain factors and to "deep-mine excavations" dug by men in black. The Almoner's own signature is on every draft.

failure.text: The ledgers are a thicket of dwarven accountancy. You will need help to read them.

actions.label: Audit the Almonry's ledgers under royal warrant

success.text: The ledgers tell it plainly once you see it: the Almonry has borrowed a fortune against the royal seal, and the money runs to Port Sorrel grain factors and to "deep-mine excavations" dug by men in black. The Almoner's own signature is on every draft.

failure.text: The ledgers are a thicket of dwarven accountancy. You will need help to read them.

actions.label: Hire a Consortium clerk to walk you through the ledgers

outcome.text: A patient old clerk takes most of a day over it. The ledgers tell it plainly once you see it: the Almonry has borrowed a fortune against the royal seal, and the money runs to Port Sorrel grain factors and to "deep-mine excavations" dug by men in black. The Almoner's own signature is on every draft.

exits.label: Take the old imperial road to Vaelthorn

scenes.name: The Sky-Towers of Old Vaelthorn
scenes.seed: The broken sky-towers of the old empire lean over a valley of white rubble, joined by bridges that no longer quite meet. Constructs still walk the terraces on errands centuries cold. At the top waits the Vault of Oaths, where the first oath-knights sealed a Tooth beneath their holy lance.

variants.seed: A rope ladder dangles from the west tower: Vosk the Hollow and his cultists are already climbing.
You are too late. The Vault of Oaths stands open and empty, and Choir hymn-marks are chalked on its door.
The tower wards are dark now, their runes gone grey.
Vosk's cultists have smashed the constructs and pried the Sky Tooth and the great lance out of the Vault with chains.
Ser Corwin is very quiet. He knows every carving on these towers from the Order's songs.
Aurek is sketching the ward-runes as fast as he can climb.

onEnter.text: You reach the foot of the sky-towers. The way up is a climb of two broken towers and a bridge between them.

actions.label: Climb to the first sky-bridge

success.text: You haul yourself up the ivy and onto the first sky-bridge. Far below, you can hear the Choir climbers.

failure.text: A handhold crumbles and you fall two storeys onto the bridge below (3d6 falling damage). The fall splits your brow; it will scar. Vosk's climbers pass you.

actions.label: Climb the last broken tower to the Vault of Oaths

success.text: You reach the Vault of Oaths ahead of the Choir. Nothing has disturbed its dust in centuries.

failure.text: The tower shrugs you off onto a ledge (3d6 falling damage). By the time you reach the Vault, Vosk the Hollow is already inside.

actions.label: Disable the tower wards

success.text: You unpick the ward-runes one by one. Deep in the vault, something huge settles back into sleep.

failure.text: A rune flares under your fingers. Deep in the vault, something huge wakes up.

actions.label: Enter the Vault of Oaths

outcome.text: Three suits of empty armor turn their helms toward you and raise their swords.

actions.label: Enter the Vault of Oaths

outcome.text: Three suits of empty armor turn their helms toward you, and behind them a shield guardian unfolds from the wall.

actions.label: Recite the First Oath and lift Dawnbreaker

success.text: You speak the First Oath of the Dawn Lance, and Dawnbreaker comes out of the stone as if it had been waiting for you. The lance is yours to carry.

failure.text: You stumble over the old words, and the lance will not move.

actions.label: Let Ser Corwin recite the First Oath

outcome.text: Corwin kneels and speaks the First Oath without a stumble. Dawnbreaker comes out of the stone into his hands, and he gives it to you to carry, very carefully. He has waited his whole life for this.

actions.label: Face Vosk the Hollow

outcome.text: Vosk the Hollow climbs through the Vault door with two fanatics at his back. His eyes are sewn shut and he sees you perfectly. "The Tooth, please. The lance you may keep; it is far too heavy."

actions.label: Take the Sky Tooth back from Vosk

outcome.text: Vosk turns from the chained lance with the Sky Tooth glowing in his fist. "Late," he says, "but welcome."

actions.label: Bind Vosk and take him alive

outcome.text: You bind Vosk's hands and gag him against spells. He hums the Choir's tune through the gag.

actions.label: Kill Vosk the Hollow

outcome.text: Vosk dies smiling, and his last breath is a note of the Choir's hymn.

actions.label: Search Vosk's notes

success.text: Among Vosk's ciphered notes is a letter in a fine, familiar hand: "Bring me the Sky Tooth before midsummer. The masque will cover everything. S." The writing is Lady Seraphine's.

failure.text: Vosk's notes are Choir cipher over imperial shorthand, and they defeat you.

exits.label: Carry the news to Dawnspire Keep
Take the old imperial road to Deepanvil Hold

scenes.name: The Vigil at Dawnspire
scenes.seed: Dawnspire Keep catches the first light on its tall spire, but its halls are half-empty since the Ashfall Winter. Lord-Commander Aldric Thane, scarred and grey, receives you in the chapel of the Lance beneath the empty rack where Dawnbreaker once hung.

variants.seed: Every knight in the chapel is staring at the lance in your hands.
You have to tell Thane that the Choir carried Dawnbreaker away.
Dawnbreaker hangs on its rack again, and the knights keep a vigil beneath it.
A freckled page in a too-big tabard runs to meet you: Pip Hallard of Millbrook, a page of the Dawn Lance now.
Corwin stands straight as a spear before his old mentor, and Thane does not look at him.
Ser Corwin wears the Lance tabard again.

onEnter.text: Thane listens to your report in silence. When you finish, he says only, "Stay the night. The Choir will know where you are by now."

actions.label: Return Dawnbreaker to the Order

outcome.text: You lay Dawnbreaker on the altar. Thane's hands shake when he lifts it. "The Order will remember this," he says, "and so will I." The Lance will ride with you when the dragon comes.

actions.label: Keep Dawnbreaker for the fight to come

outcome.text: You keep the lance. Thane says nothing, which is worse than anything he could have said. The knights will not meet your eye.

actions.label: Refuse Corwin and keep Dawnbreaker

outcome.text: Corwin demands the lance back in the Order's name, before the whole chapel. You refuse him. The Order will not forgive this.

actions.label: Tell Thane that the Choir has Dawnbreaker

outcome.text: Thane hears it standing up. "Then we will take it back from them," he says, "or die in the attempt, as the Order always has."

actions.label: Ask Thane to reinstate Ser Corwin

success.text: Thane hears you out, then draws his sword and lays it on Corwin's shoulder. "Rise, Ser Corwin of the Dawn Lance. Again."

failure.text: "The Order dismissed him for cause," says Thane. Corwin says nothing at all.

actions.label: Sleep, with Pip on watch

outcome.text: Pip shakes you awake in the dark: "There are men on the chapel roof, and the shadows are wrong." You are on your feet before the assassins reach the door.

actions.label: Keep watch through the night

success.text: In the small hours you hear a tile slide on the chapel roof, and the shadows start to move without their owners. You are ready.

failure.text: You wake with a poisoned blade already in your shoulder. The wound will leave black veins that never fade.

exits.label: Ride for the Almoner's midsummer masque

scenes.name: The Almoner's Midsummer Masque
scenes.seed: The Almonry's gardens glitter with a thousand lanterns. Nobles in golden masks dance under the midsummer stars, and the Queen herself sits in a bower of white roses. Lady Seraphine, masked as a dove, rises to sing for her guests.

variants.seed: Your mask hides a face that is on every wanted poster in the city.
The first note of Seraphine's song stops your heart. You have heard this voice before, in the dream beneath the Millbrook barrow.
A tall guest in a sea-captain's coat and a gull mask is watching you. Harrow Vey is a guest of the Almonry tonight.
The evidence you carry would hang any noble in the kingdom.
Aurek grips your arm when his aunt begins to sing. He is shaking.
Pip has come along as your "page", wearing a mask three sizes too big.

onEnter.text: You are admitted to the masque in borrowed finery. Somewhere among the golden masks is the Choir, and somewhere among its hymns is the voice from your dreams.

actions.label: Dance and sing your way into the crowd

success.text: You dance three sets and sing one chorus, and the masked Choir watchers stop looking at you.

failure.text: You tread on a duchess. Three masks turn to watch you for the rest of the night.

actions.label: Pass yourself off as a minor noble

success.text: You are the Baron of somewhere nobody has heard of, and nobody wants to admit it. The Choir watchers lose interest.

failure.text: Nobody believes in your barony. Three masks turn to watch you for the rest of the night.

actions.label: Listen to Seraphine's song

success.text: Under the sweetness, it is the same voice that sings in the Choir's hymns: *you will never want again*. Seraphine Vell is the Cantor.

failure.text: It is a beautiful song, and it tells you nothing.

actions.label: Listen to the voice from your dream

success.text: It is the voice from beneath the Millbrook barrow, the one that promised you would never want again. Seraphine Vell is the Cantor.

failure.text: For a moment you are sure, and then the song ends and you are not.

actions.label: Tell Aurek what you know about his aunt, before anyone else

outcome.text: Aurek listens with his mask in his hands. "I knew," he says at last. "I think I have known for a year. Thank you for telling me first."

actions.label: Accuse Lady Seraphine before the court

outcome.text: You stop the music and lay out the evidence, piece by piece, before the Queen. The court turns to look at Seraphine, and for one moment the Cantor's mask slips: she smiles. Then the lanterns go out, and she is gone.

actions.label: Accuse Lady Seraphine before the court

success.text: Your evidence is thin, but you make the court listen. The Queen turns to her godmother and asks her to answer. Seraphine smiles, and the lanterns go out, and she is gone.

failure.text: The court laughs, and then it stops laughing. Chamberlain Hale calls the palace guard to seize the lunatic who slandered the Almoner.

actions.label: Accuse Lady Seraphine before the court

outcome.text: You have a feeling and no proof. Seraphine looks hurt, the Queen looks angry, and Chamberlain Hale calls the palace guard to seize you.

actions.label: Confront Seraphine privately in the rose garden

outcome.text: You find her alone among the roses. She does not deny it. "You have seen the fen, and the fever wards," she says. "Can you truly tell me hunger should go on forever?" Then she steps back into the dark of the garden, and she is gone.

actions.label: Say nothing and watch her

outcome.text: You say nothing and dance on. But Seraphine meets your eyes across the garden and knows that you know. Before midnight she is gone, and the Queen has collapsed in her bower of roses.

actions.label: Enjoy the masque

outcome.text: The masque goes on until midnight. Then a scream: the Queen has collapsed in her bower of roses, and the Almoner is nowhere to be found.

actions.label: Wait for Aurek

outcome.text: Near midnight Aurek comes down the dungeon stair with a stolen key and a very bad excuse for the guards. "The Queen has collapsed," he whispers. "My aunt is gone. I need you."

actions.label: Break out of the Highcrown dungeons

success.text: You tear a rusted grate out of the cell floor and follow the drain up into the palace catacombs, where the whole palace is shouting that the Queen has fallen.

failure.text: The grate holds, and the guard laughs.

actions.label: Wait out the night in the cells

outcome.text: Three days pass before a frightened Chamberlain Hale unlocks your cell. The Queen has been poisoned, the Almoner has vanished, and suddenly your slander does not sound so mad.

scenes.name: The Palace Undercroft
scenes.seed: Beneath the palace, the old catacombs of the Varannis kings run down into the hill. Above, bells are ringing: Queen Isolde has collapsed, grey-lipped and humming a tune she has never learned. Below, the Choir is covering its mistress's escape.

variants.seed: Seraphine was warned. She left the masque an hour before you moved, and the catacombs are already full of her rearguard.
Three days late, the trail is cold, and something has made its nest in the catacombs.
The whole court saw the Almoner unmasked, and the palace guard follows you down the stair.
You are still an outlaw in these halls, and the guards are hunting you as hard as the Choir.
You know this sickness, and you know its cure.
Liesel's locket is cold in your hand: a little girl's face, and the name "Liesel, Cinderdale".

onEnter.text: Seraphine's parting gift was a kiss on her goddaughter's cheek, and a concentrated dose of the Whispering Sickness. You can save the Queen, or chase the Cantor into the dark while the trail is warm; you will not have time for both.

actions.label: Cut through the Choir rearguard

outcome.text: Ghasts in Almonry livery and Choir fanatics block the catacomb stair, and the shadows on the walls move without their owners.

actions.label: Fight through the Choir ambush

outcome.text: The rearguard was waiting for you: ghasts drop from the ossuary shelves and the shadows close in.

actions.label: Treat the Queen with the fen cure

outcome.text: You know this sickness. Bell-ash, bitterroot and a Briarkin chant: by dawn the Queen stops humming and asks for water.

actions.label: Fight for the Queen's life

success.text: You bleed the spores out of her and keep her breathing through the worst of the night. At dawn, Isolde opens her eyes.

failure.text: You slow the poison, but you cannot stop it. Isolde lingers, grey and humming. The court physicians say she may last until the next moon.

actions.label: Pursue the Cantor into the catacombs

outcome.text: You leave the Queen to her physicians and run into the dark after her godmother. Behind you, Isolde starts to hum.

actions.label: Sprint down the ossuary stair

success.text: You take the ossuary stair three steps at a time and hear her footsteps ahead.

failure.text: You slip on old bones and lose her footsteps.

actions.label: Vault the collapsed crypt

success.text: You vault the fallen crypt-lids and come down running.

failure.text: The crypt-lids shift under you and you go down hard.

actions.label: Force the drowned gate

success.text: You heave the flooded gate open against the water, and there is her lantern.

failure.text: The drowned gate will not move; you lose minutes finding another way.

actions.label: Run the ledge above the cistern

success.text: You run the cistern ledge without looking down, and there is her lantern.

failure.text: You fall into the cistern and lose minutes climbing out.

actions.label: Climb after her up the well-shaft

success.text: You catch her cloak at the top of the well-shaft.

failure.text: Your hands slip on the wet stones of the well-shaft.

actions.label: Leap for her across the broken bridge

success.text: You leap the broken bridge and catch her cloak.

failure.text: You leap for the broken bridge and fall short.

actions.label: Stand before the court as the woman who unmasked the Cantor

outcome.text: At dawn a note is found pinned to the Almoner's empty chair: "The dragon will do what the Choir cannot. Hungry things always come home." In the east, the Emberpeaks are smoking. (Milestone: chapter complete.)

actions.label: Slip out of Highcrown before the watch finds you

outcome.text: You go over the palace wall at dawn with the watch at your heels. Behind you, a note is found on the Almoner's empty chair: "The dragon will do what the Choir cannot. Hungry things always come home." In the east, the Emberpeaks are smoking.

actions.label: Keep what you know, and prepare

outcome.text: The court says the Almoner was taken by the Choir. You know better. On her empty chair, a note: "The dragon will do what the Choir cannot. Hungry things always come home." In the east, the Emberpeaks are smoking.

actions.label: Leave the palace to its mourning

outcome.text: The court mourns its vanished Almoner, taken, everyone says, by the Choir. A note on her empty chair reads only: "The dragon will do what the Choir cannot. Hungry things always come home." In the east, the Emberpeaks are smoking.

npcs.name: Queen Isolde Varannis
npcs.personality: A young, sharp-witted queen who inherited an empty treasury and trusts too few advisers. Proud, generous to allies, and fiercely loyal to her godmother.
secrets: Owes the Ironvault Consortium more than the Crown can pay.
Seraphine raised her after her mother died; she cannot imagine her godmother lying to her.
npcs.voice: Crisp and quick, a little too formal, with sudden flashes of dry humour.

npcs.name: Lady Seraphine Vell
npcs.personality: The Royal Almoner: warm, tireless, beloved by the poor, godmother to the Queen. In truth she is the Cantor of the Hollow Choir, a zealot who believes Vashkul will devour hunger itself.
secrets: She starved in Cinderdale in the Ashfall Winter; her little sister Liesel died in her arms.
She truly loves Isolde and means to "spare" her by converting her.
npcs.voice: Soft, low and kind; never raises her voice; her singing voice is the voice of the Choir.

npcs.name: Chamberlain Oberin Hale
npcs.personality: Pompous, loyal to the Crown to the bone, and deeply suspicious of adventurers who arrive with pirate friends and ancient relics.
secrets: Has warned the Queen twice that the Almonry spends too freely, and been laughed at.
npcs.voice: Plummy and slow; speaks of himself as "the Chamberlain".

npcs.name: Aurek Vell
npcs.personality: A brilliant, anxious young Veyran scholar, kind to a fault, who craves his aunt's approval and suspects her of something he cannot bear to name.
secrets: His aunt vanishes on the nights the Choir sings.
His late father studied "reverse-singing" the Teeth; the research is hidden in the Almonry library.
npcs.voice: Rapid, precise and apologetic, prone to footnotes.

npcs.name: Vosk the Hollow
npcs.personality: A renegade Veyran scholar and the Choir's archivist-mage, eyes sewn shut, courteous and utterly without pity.
secrets: Carries letters from the Cantor in Seraphine's own hand.
npcs.voice: Dry and scholarly; hums the Choir's tune between sentences.

npcs.name: Lord-Commander Aldric Thane
npcs.personality: A scarred veteran of the Ashfall Winter who lost his lance and half his knights. Honourable to a fault and slow to forgive.
secrets: He gave the order to abandon Cinderdale in the Ashfall Winter.
npcs.voice: Gravel and silence; says little, means all of it.

npcs.name: Pip Hallard
npcs.personality: The miller's son from Millbrook, rescued from the barrow, now a page of the Dawn Lance and utterly devoted to the hero.
npcs.voice: Breathless and eager; calls the hero "my lord" or "my lady" whatever they say.

npcs.name: Guildmistress Brunhild Ashgrove
npcs.personality: A shrewd dwarf who measures every favor in coin and never forgets a debt. Honest, but never generous.
secrets: The Almonry's loans frighten her: no charity borrows like that.
npcs.voice: Blunt, clipped, counts on her fingers while she talks.

win.text: You fight clear of the watch and vanish into the lower city.

lose.text: You wake in the Highcrown dungeons. A turnkey tells you the Queen may hear your case in three days, or may not.

flee.text: You break away into the crowd outside the walls. The gate is still shut to you.

win.text: The mine is clear. On the grimlocks' bodies you find Almonry pay-chits: the "diggers in black" were delvers the Choir blinded and set to dig. Ashgrove pays her debts: the ledgers are yours, and so is a reward from the Ironvault.

lose.text: Dwarven miners haul you out of the dark by your ankles. The mine is still lost.

flee.text: You retreat up the shaft with the grimlocks' hooting behind you.

encounters.name: The guardians of the Vault of Oaths

win.text: The last suit of armor kneels, as if to a knight, and falls apart.

lose.text: You wake among the rubble eight hours later. The constructs are smashed, the Vault stands open, and the Sky Tooth is gone: Vosk took it while you lay there. The lance is still in the stone.

flee.text: You retreat down the tower stair. The constructs do not follow; they never have.

win.text: The shield guardian folds back into the wall, and the last suit of armor falls apart.

lose.text: You wake among the rubble eight hours later. The constructs are smashed, the Vault stands open, and the Sky Tooth is gone: Vosk took it while you lay there. The lance is still in the stone.

flee.text: You retreat down the tower stair. The constructs do not follow; they never have.

encounters.name: Vosk the Hollow
terrain: the open sky beyond the broken wall

win.text: Vosk's fanatics fall, and Vosk kneels on the Vault floor, spent, his hands open.

lose.text: You wake with the lance still in your arms: Vosk could not lift it, and did not try. The Sky Tooth is gone with him.

flee.text: You break away down the towers with Dawnbreaker and the Sky Tooth. Vosk lets you go; he has other errands.

encounters.name: Vosk at the Vault of Oaths
terrain: the open sky beyond the broken wall

win.text: Vosk falls to his knees among the chains, and the Sky Tooth rolls from his hand. Dawnbreaker lies free in its chains: you take them both.

lose.text: You wake alone in the ruined Vault. Vosk's cultists have dragged Dawnbreaker away in its chains, and Vosk has the Sky Tooth.

flee.text: You fall back down the towers. By the time you look back, Vosk's cultists are hauling Dawnbreaker away in its chains, and Vosk has the Sky Tooth.

win.text: The last assassin dies on the chapel steps. Sewn into his collar is an Almonry masque token.

lose.text: The knights carry you to the chapel. The assassins fled when the bells rang.

flee.text: You fall back into the keep and bar the doors until the knights come. The assassins melt into the night.

win.text: The last assassin dies on the chapel steps. Sewn into his collar is an Almonry masque token.

lose.text: The knights carry you to the chapel. The assassins fled when the bells rang.

win.text: You fight free of the guard without killing anyone. Then a scream: the Queen has collapsed in her bower, and the Almoner is gone. You follow her trail down into the palace catacombs.

lose.text: You wake in the Highcrown dungeons, bruised, disarmed and branded a slanderer.

flee.text: You break away into the dark of the gardens. Then a scream: the Queen has collapsed, and the Almoner is gone. You follow her trail down into the catacombs.

win.text: The rearguard is broken. Her footsteps are still echoing below; the Queen's breathing is failing above.

lose.text: You wake in the palace chapel. The Cantor is long gone.

flee.text: You fall back up the stair and bar the catacomb door. The Cantor is long gone.

win.text: The ambush is broken, but the Cantor is long gone. Above, the Queen's breathing is failing.

lose.text: You wake in the palace chapel. The Cantor is long gone.

flee.text: You fall back up the stair and bar the catacomb door. The Cantor is long gone.

beats.text: Aurek takes you aside, white-faced. "My aunt goes out on the nights the Choir sings. Every time. I have been telling myself it is charity work."
Two threads now lead to the Almonry. If you could only hear the Cantor’s voice, you would be sure.
You have enough evidence now to accuse the Royal Almoner before the court.
The voice and the evidence agree. Lady Seraphine Vell, the Royal Almoner, is the Cantor of the Hollow Choir.
As the court breaks up, a young Veyran scholar in ink-stained cuffs approaches you: Aurek Vell, the Almoner's nephew, with "strange readings" from his aunt's library.
Seraphine takes your hand in both of hers. "We have met, in a sense," she says, and smiles, and for a moment the Tooth of Want seems to hum somewhere far away.
The Queen commends you before the whole court for exposing Governor Pell.
On the Saltwind Company's letter of praise, the Queen grants you a royal warrant to investigate without being asked.
Chamberlain Hale reminds the court that you sailed with Red Gull pirates. Every request you make here will be weighed twice.
The Almonry clerk carries the Tooth of Want away. You will not see it again soon.
The Almonry clerk carries the Drowned Tooth away. You will not see it again soon.
The Almonry clerk carries the Briar Tooth away. You will not see it again soon.
The Almonry clerk carries the Brass Tooth away. You will not see it again soon.
The Almonry clerk carries the Singing Tooth away. You will not see it again soon.
Beneath where the lance stood lies the Sky Tooth, humming like a struck bell. You take it.
Old Vaelthorn has given up its secrets, one way or another.
The sky-towers of Vaelthorn have tested you. (Milestone: level 6.)
Corwin kneels before Thane and asks to be taken back into the Order, here and now, away from you. "I cannot follow you further," he says. He stays at Dawnspire.
Thane lifts Dawnbreaker, then lays it on Corwin's shoulder. "The lance came home in your hands, Ser Corwin. Rise a knight of the Dawn Lance, again."
Pip took a knife meant for you. The chaplain says he will live, and he will carry the scar proudly.
Aurek slips away from your side during the second dance. Too late, you see him whispering at his aunt's ear. When you look again, Seraphine is watching you, and Aurek is gone. He has warned her.
Aurek stands frozen while the court stares at his family. "You could have told me first," he says, and will not look at you.
Without a cure, the court physicians can only slow the Sickness. The Queen lingers, grey and humming.
The court physicians know the fen cure now, and they use it. The Queen will live.

You catch Seraphine at the mouth of the catacombs, above the river. She tears free and is gone into the dark water, but her cloak stays in your hands, and something falls from it: a child's locket, engraved "Liesel, Cinderdale".
Her lantern goes out ahead of you, and the catacombs are silent. The Cantor has escaped.
In the Cantor's abandoned satchel you find the Sky Tooth. You have taken it back.
In the Cantor's abandoned satchel you find the Singing Tooth, the Tooth you trusted her with.
In the Cantor's abandoned satchel you find the Brass Tooth, the Tooth you trusted her with.
In the Cantor's abandoned satchel you find the Briar Tooth, the Tooth you trusted her with.
In the Cantor's abandoned satchel you find the Drowned Tooth, the Tooth you trusted her with.
In the Cantor's abandoned satchel you find the Tooth of Want, the Tooth you trusted her with.
In the Cantor's abandoned satchel you find the Singing Tooth. You have taken it back from the Choir.
In the Cantor's abandoned satchel you find the Brass Tooth. You have taken it back from the Choir.
In the Cantor's abandoned satchel you find the Briar Tooth. You have taken it back from the Choir.
In the Cantor's abandoned satchel you find the Drowned Tooth. You have taken it back from the Choir.
In the Cantor's abandoned satchel you find the Tooth of Want. You have taken it back from the Choir.
You have faced the Cantor in her own house. (Milestone: level 7.)

deadlines.text: Reach the Vault of Oaths at Old Vaelthorn before Vosk the Hollow
deadlines.warning: A day left: Vosk's climbers will reach the Vault of Oaths by tomorrow.

missed.text: Too late: Vosk the Hollow has reached the Vault of Oaths. His cultists have hauled Dawnbreaker away in chains, and Vosk has the Sky Tooth.

endings.name: The Mask Falls
endings.text: You unmasked the Cantor before the whole court. The Crown knows its enemy now, and will muster openly against her.

endings.name: What the Hero Knows
endings.text: You know who the Cantor is, but the court does not. Whatever comes next, you will have to gather allies quietly.

endings.name: Hunted in Highcrown
endings.text: The Cantor is free, and you are the one the Crown is hunting. Only her own flight can clear your name now.

endings.name: The Almoner Vanishes
endings.text: The Almoner is gone, and the court believes the Choir took her. The truth is still waiting for someone to find it.
